questions.question: How does Redux Toolkit work? Explain createSlice and configureStore.
questions.title: Redux Toolkit Explained — createSlice, configureStore & Immer
questions.direct_answer:
How does Redux Toolkit work? Explain createSlice and configureStore.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** createSlice auto-generates actions + reducer with Immer; configureStore wires middleware/devtools; RTK Query for data fetching.

**Classic weak answer:** Still writing hand-rolled switch-statement reducers — Redux Toolkit is the recommended default as of 2020.

**Senior finish:** Show a todo slice with createSlice, an extraReducer for async thunks, and an RTK Query endpoint for fetching.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Redux Toolkit Explained — createSlice, configureStore & Immer** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** How does Redux Toolkit work? Explain createSlice and configureStore.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **createSlice auto-generates actions + reducer with Immer; configureStore wires middleware/devtools; RTK Query for data fetching**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Still writing hand-rolled switch-statement reducers — Redux Toolkit is the recommended default as of 2020**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Show a todo slice with createSlice, an extraReducer for async thunks, and an RTK Query endpoint for fetching**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** createSlice auto-generates actions + reducer with Immer; configureStore wires middleware/devtools; RTK Query for data fetching
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

```mermaid
    COMMIT --> EF[useEffect after paint]

    end
    DIFF --> MEMO
```

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **still writing hand-rolled switch-statement reducers — Redux Toolkit is the recommended default as of 2020** and what you do instead.

questions.question: How do you use createAsyncThunk in Redux Toolkit?
questions.title: createAsyncThunk in Redux Toolkit — Async Actions Explained
questions.direct_answer:
How do you use createAsyncThunk in Redux Toolkit?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the framework runtime (render, reconciliation, DI, CD) and the browser), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Auto-generates pending/fulfilled/rejected action types; thunk function receives (arg, thunkApi); handled via extraReducers.

**Classic weak answer:** Not using rejectWithValue for custom errors — default rejection gives the raw Error, losing server payloads.

**Senior finish:** Compare with RTK Query (preferred for data fetching) and show a typical authLogin thunk.
